findings.title: raw_html posts are stored and rendered with no sanitization (stored XSS)
findings.body: `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == raw_html`, so none of the normal cooking or sanitizing pipeline runs. The content comes from remote sources. In `PollFeed` it is `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)`, which turns escaped entities such as `<script>` back into live markup. In `import_remote` it is the readability output. Nothing in `TopicEmbed.import` or `absolutize_urls` strips scripts, event handlers, or `javascript:` links. The result is written to `posts.cooked`, shown on the main site, and emitted via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in the embed iframe, which is served from the Discourse origin with `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL`. A compromised or malicious feed or page can therefore run script in Discourse's origin. The imported HTML should be sanitized with a whitelist before it is saved or served.

findings.title: `<%- end if %>` is invalid ERB/Ruby and breaks the best template
findings.body: The `if/else` opened on line 2 is closed with `end if`, a modifier `if` with no condition. Erubis appends `;` after a statement tag, which yields `end if ;`. That is a syntax error, or at best an `if` conditioned on the next emitted output statement. Either way the template cannot render correctly, so `embed/best` fails whenever a topic already exists. It should be `<%- end %>`. The controller specs do not render views, so nothing catches this.

findings.title: Wrapping PostCreator in Topic.transaction defeats its after-commit job enqueueing
findings.body: `PostCreator#create` deliberately enqueues `process_post` and `feature_topic_users` after its own transaction commits (see the comment in `enqueue_jobs`). Wrapping the call in an outer `Topic.transaction` means those jobs are enqueued before the outer transaction commits, which now also includes `TopicEmbed.create!`. In production a Sidekiq worker can pick up `process_post` before the post row is visible and fail or skip processing. It also makes the rollback semantics unclear, because the `ActiveRecord::Rollback` raised inside PostCreator's nested transaction does not roll back the outer one.

findings.title: Failed post creation is not detected before creating the TopicEmbed
findings.body: `PostCreator#create` returns `@post` even when it failed and rolled back, for example on host-spam detection or a save failure. That post is unsaved, so `post.present?` is still true. `TopicEmbed.create!` then runs with `post_id: nil` and `topic_id: nil`, which raises a NOT NULL violation. This surfaces as a confusing exception in the job instead of a clean failure. The guard should check `post.persisted?` or `post.errors.blank?`. The update branch has a related problem: `embed.post` can be nil if the post was deleted, and `PostRevisor.new(nil)` then blows up.

findings.title: Kernel#open on a URL string allows command execution and unchecked fetches
findings.body: `open(url)` is `Kernel#open` with open-uri loaded, so a string starting with `|` runs a shell command. `import_remote` does not validate its argument itself. Only the `TopicRetriever` path checks the host. The Disqus thor task passes `t[:link]` straight from an XML export, and `PollFeed` does `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` the same way. Use `URI.parse(url).open`, or RestClient, after verifying the scheme is http or https, and set explicit timeouts. `open-uri` is also only required in `poll_feed.rb`, so `import_remote` can fail with ENOENT if that file has not been loaded.

findings.title: import mutates its input and interpolates the URL into HTML unescaped
findings.body: `contents << ...` appends the footer to the caller's string in place. Callers that reuse the string, such as the memoized `let(:contents)` in the spec, see it change. The URL is also placed into `#{url}` without escaping. The only validation is `/^https?:\/\//`, which uses `^` rather than `\A`, so a multi-line value with `http://` on a later line passes. A `'` or `<` in the URL can inject attributes or markup into a post that is never sanitized. Build a new string, escape the URL, and anchor the regex with `\A`.

findings.title: absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs and ignores other relative forms
findings.body: `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative links such as `//cdn.example.com/x.jpg`. `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, giving `http://host/cdn.example.com/x.jpg`, which is a broken link. The same happens for `img src` on line 71. Relative paths without a leading slash (`images/a.png`, `../a.png`) are left untouched, and the code resolves against only scheme and host rather than the article URL. The port check (`!= 80 && != 443`) is also wrong for https on 80 or http on 443. `URI.join(url, href)` handles all of these correctly.

findings.title: One bad feed item aborts the whole poll (nil content, no per-item rescue)
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when an item has no `content`, which is common for RSS 2.0 feeds that only carry `description`. The loop has no per-item rescue, so one such item, or an exception from `TopicEmbed.import` (such as `create!` validation or a DB error on a long title), stops the import of every item after it. The job runs with `retry: false`, so the same item blocks the feed on every hourly run. Fall back to `description` when `content` is nil, and rescue and log errors per item.

findings.title: Throttle is keyed on the full URL and non-atomic, so it is trivially bypassed
findings.body: The key is `retrieved:#{@embed_url}`, so varying the query string (`?a=1`, `?a=2`, ...) on the allowed host gets a fresh throttle slot each time. Each one triggers a full `Jobs::PollFeed` run (fetch, parse and import of the whole feed) when feed polling is enabled, plus a remote HTTP fetch and a new topic via `import_remote`. This allows request amplification and duplicate topics per URL variant. The embed URL should be canonicalized, and there should be a global limit on retrievals. Separately, `setnx` followed by `expire` is not atomic. A crash between the two leaves a key that never expires and blocks that URL permanently. Use `SET key val NX EX 60`.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring match
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test. Any origin that is a substring of the configured URL passes. For example, with `discourseUrl = 'http://forum.example.com/'`, a message from origin `http://forum.example.co` is accepted. Compare `e.origin` for equality against the origin parsed from `discourseUrl`.

findings.title: Request referer interpolated into an inline JS string as the targetOrigin
findings.body: `request.referer` is attacker-influenced (path and query are free-form) and is only HTML-escaped inside a `<script>` block, where entities are not decoded. A trailing backslash in the referer escapes the closing quote and breaks the script, so the resize message is never sent. HTML-escaping is also the wrong encoding for a JS context, and `&` sequences end up in the string. `postMessage` expects an origin, so emit `scheme://host[:port]` derived server-side and serialize it with `to_json` or `j`.

findings.title: `force: true` in migrations drops an existing table
findings.body: `create_table ..., force: true` runs `DROP TABLE` first if the table exists. Here it is in the new `topic_embeds` migration and in the edited `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`. The latter is an already-applied migration unrelated to this feature, and the edit has no effect except when the migration is re-run, when it silently destroys data. Remove `force: true` from the new migration and leave the old migration untouched.

findings.title: Disqus import silently drops the --category option and original thread dates
findings.body: The `-c/--category` option and its lookup are removed, and topic creation now goes through `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which takes no category or `created_at`. Existing users of the task lose category placement and the original topic timestamps. Each import now also performs a live HTTP fetch of the thread link, so the task fails or produces content from the live site if the link is dead. This is a behaviour change unrelated to the embed feature and is not mentioned in the PR.

findings.title: Controller specs pass for the wrong reason and miss the key access check
findings.body: 'is 404 without an embed_url' does not set `embeddable_host`, so `ensure_embeddable` raises InvalidAccess before `params.require` is reached. The test passes without exercising the missing-parameter path. `should_not be_success` is also too weak to tell the cases apart. There is no test for a referer whose host differs from `embeddable_host`, which is the central security check, and none for a malformed referer. Nothing covers the `loading` branch.

findings.title: New gems added to the Gemfile but only the rails4 lockfile was updated
findings.body: `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` were added for both Rails 3 and Rails 4 boot modes, but only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` was updated. If a separate `Gemfile.lock` exists for the Rails 3 mode, it is now out of sync, and `bundle install --deployment` or frozen installs there will fail.
